title: An expanded document audit found training matches for 35.2% of test pages
summary: An expanded audit of the RVL-CDIP benchmark found training-set matches for 14,076 test pages, or 35.20%, and 14,151 validation pages, or 35.38%. The search used learned image matching and counted near-duplicates that shared a document template as well as copies. A smaller 2023 analysis had already identified substantial duplication.

source_review.scope: June arXiv v1 front matter, §§4.1–4.2 learned matching and Table 3; October v1 extension introduction and stated matching result; EACL 2023 §5 sampled overlap estimate.

evidence.tested: Learned CLIP embeddings proposed likely cross-split matches before SuperPoint and LightGlue visual matching and a text-similarity check. The calibration set contained 403 matched pairs among 1,600 candidate pairs, with 82.9% recall at the chosen threshold.
evidence.unknown: The audit includes same-template pages and may miss matches. The earlier 2023 sample-based estimate of about 32% uses a different method and is not a baseline for measuring a change in duplication.
evidence.ai_role: Learned CLIP embeddings screen scanned documents for likely matching pairs, and SuperPoint and LightGlue match their visual structure before final duplicate classification.
